question: Can contributors evaluate keys, meaning maps, conjectures, restorations and segmentations through the same source-linked commands and controls?
outcome: Five versioned task commands and selftest implemented. Fifty numerical comparisons match their source endpoints, including published-key gain, Shot B's frozen combined score, historical split counts, Markov2 recovery, three release row/page scorers and readable-cohort segmentation baselines. A new seed retains the original closure and records prior statistic-family exposure.
challenge: The earlier methods use different units and input formats. Release wrappers import Parquet dependencies, line breaks provide only positive labels, shared confirmation reads require a round-wide freeze, and the current corrected line-face list differs from the older reviewed list.
remedy: Imported core project scorers with path/hash records, read the release's original JSON parents, preserved partial-label scoring, froze every registered shot before reads, recorded spending and wrote the corrected 69-face line re-score separately. Generated controls exercise nominal rejection, power, input errors and loader guards.
retry_when: A changed scorer, source representation, independently acquired object population or explicitly declared joint planting law requires a new source-pinned run. Preserve all October 13 endpoints.
